name: Greek Yogurt Bowl
why: Breakfast when you do not want to cook and do not want another egg. Three minutes, one bowl, no heat.

serves.proteinMath: 19 g from 200 g of Greek yogurt (11 g per 115 g, off the label). About 4 g from 30 g of raw oats (roughly 13 g protein per 100 g, a standard rolled-oats figure). Honey and the frozen fruit add well under a gram. Total about 23 g. The optional 1 tsp of cocoa and 1 tbsp of peanut butter add roughly 5 g more if you use them, and a scoop of whey stirred in on top of that makes it 51 g.

steps.text: Put 200 g of Greek yogurt in a bowl. That is about three quarters of a cup, or a quarter of the tub.
steps.look: Weigh it once on the new scale and look at how far up the bowl it comes. After that you will never need to weigh it again.

steps.text: Add 1 handful of frozen berries or mango straight from the freezer and stir them through.
steps.look: They thaw in the yogurt in about 10 minutes and release juice into it, which is the point. If you want it ready now, microwave the fruit alone for 20 seconds first.

steps.text: Scatter 30 g of raw oats over the top and drizzle 1 tsp of honey. If you want it, stir in 1 tsp of cocoa powder and 1 tbsp of peanut butter too.
steps.look: Raw oats straight from the bag, no cooking. They soften slightly in the yogurt and give it something to chew. About 23 g of protein as written: 19 g from 200 g of yogurt (11 g per 115 g, off the label), about 4 g from the oats. The cocoa and peanut butter add roughly 5 g more if you use them. Stir a scoop of whey in on top of that and it is 51 g.

provenance.statement: WRITTEN BY AN AGENT. No published source. Nobody has cooked these quantities. Treat every number as a first draft. There is no heat or doneness judgment anywhere in this one, which is why it is offered despite having no source: nothing here can burn.
